entry.title: Cary Institute Study Links Acorns and Mouse Populations to Lyme Disease Risk
entry.content:
Links: sciencedaily.com

A 35-year ecological study conducted by researchers at the Cary Institute of Ecosystem Studies, published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, reveals that white-footed mouse populations and oak tree acorn production are significantly stronger predictors of nymphal tick abundance than white-tailed deer populations. The long-term data show that heavy acorn crops provide abundant food for forest rodents, enabling mouse populations to surge and subsequently drive up nymphal tick numbers two years later.

Despite the clear link between mice and overall tick abundance, high mouse populations do not consistently predict a higher proportion of infected ticks, as other lesser-transmitting host species dilute the pathogen's prevalence within the ecosystem. Furthermore, the findings indicate that blacklegged ticks survive temperature extremes more effectively than previously assumed by sheltering in soil and leaf litter, complicating traditional assumptions about how weather and deer impact Lyme disease exposure.

entry.title: Examining Nondeterminism in the Futhark Programming Language
entry.content:
Links: futhark-lang.org | lobsters

The Futhark programming language blog examines the origins of nondeterminism within its parallel execution model, identifying two primary sources: language abuse through unsafe constructs like unchecked scatter operations, and floating-point roundoff errors caused by non-associative operations. While Futhark is generally characterized as a deterministic language, parallel reductions and scans alter the order of floating-point additions depending on hardware schedules, leading to replayable or approximate results.

Although fully deterministic implementations—such as tree-based summation—are possible, they incur significant performance penalties compared to hardware-optimized routines that rely on atomic instructions or backend-specific chunking. The post highlights that sacrificing strict determinism is a deliberate design choice required to maintain high performance on modern parallel hardware, balancing numerical consistency against execution speed.

entry.title: Analysis of Deno Security Model and Permission System Limitations
entry.content:

An essay by developer Goldstein critiques the Deno JavaScript runtime's security model, arguing that its built-in permission system is fundamentally flawed and provides a false sense of security. The piece details how Deno's approach emulates operating system security controls at the standard library level rather than properly sandboxing the underlying process.

The analysis highlights specific attack vectors, including terminal prompt manipulation via in-band data streams and bypasses of granular execution permissions like `--allow-run` through environment variables such as `PATH` and `LD_PRELOAD`. Because most system binaries and editors are highly configurable, relying on partial runtime restrictions is insufficient, leading the author to recommend traditional OS-level sandboxing tools like bubblewrap instead of Deno's runtime permissions.

entry.content:
Links: mitchellh.com | lobsters | hacker news

Mitchell Hashimoto has released libghostty-vt 1.0, a portable, high-performance C library for terminal emulation extracted directly from the core of the Ghostty project. The 1.0 milestone establishes a stable C ABI and semantic versioning, ensuring long-term compatibility for dynamic linking and operating system distribution packaging.

The library has already achieved widespread production adoption across millions of users in applications such as JetBrains IDEs, Neovim, and various developer tools. Built with a minimal, permissively licensed dependency tree and extensive cross-platform support spanning Linux, macOS, Windows, mobile platforms, and WebAssembly, it provides a generalized foundation for building terminal software.

entry.title: European Commission Accuses TikTok of Violating Digital Services Act via Harmful Content "Rabbit Holes"
entry.content:
Links: therecord.media | ec.europa.eu | hacker news

The European Commission has issued preliminary findings that TikTok violated the Digital Services Act (DSA) by using recommendation algorithms that drive users into "rabbit holes" of harmful content. The investigation found that TikTok's "For You" feed can repeatedly present users with videos related to sadness, self-harm, and body image issues based on implicit engagement signals.

This marks the first time EU regulators have directly challenged the engagement-based recommendation models of a major social media platform. If these findings are confirmed, TikTok faces potential fines of up to 6% of its annual global revenue.

entry.title: DOJ Charges Three Foreign Nationals in $129M AI Impersonation Scheme
entry.content:
Links: nbcnews.com | justice.gov

Federal prosecutors charged three foreign nationals—Jacob Soall, Sharon Hazan, and Guy Sheetrit—with orchestrating an international fraud scheme that used artificial intelligence to impersonate corporate executives and attorneys. Between July 2024 and February 2026, the group allegedly tricked employees at multiple global companies into wiring more than $129 million to accounts controlled by the conspirators.

The suspects reportedly used cloned voices and fabricated legal identities to convince accounting personnel to execute confidential financial transactions, subsequently laundering the stolen funds through cryptocurrency conversions. All three defendants face multiple counts of wire fraud, aggravated identity theft, and money laundering, with each charge carrying a maximum sentence of 20 years in prison.

entry.title: Tech Executives and OpenAI Express Concern Over Anti-Data Center Election Results
entry.content:
Links: wsj.com

Tech executives gathered at an election-night event hosted by Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang expressed significant concern over local election results and ballot measures targeting data centers. The outcomes threaten to rein in the rapid expansion of artificial intelligence infrastructure across the United States.

Concurrently, senior leaders at OpenAI discussed whether the political resistance requires resetting expectations for the company's data center capacity and infrastructure plans by 2027. The growing local pushback highlights mounting community friction regarding the immense energy and land demands of upcoming AI projects.
